extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and potential commenters on Federal Register AI notices (industry, academia, research organizations, investors, nonprofits, state/local/tribal governments, and other interested parties)
extracted.subtask_description: A collected listing of Federal Register documents (notices, RFIs, proposed/final rules, presidential documents) related to artificial intelligence, assembled to identify opportunities and instructions for public comment and participation in AI-related rulemaking and policy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit feedback on structuring DOE partnerships for AI data curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit feedback from industry, think tanks, investors, research organizations, and other stakeholders on how DOE should best structure and enable partnerships to curate DOE scientific data across the National Laboratory complex for use in artificial intelligence (AI) models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RFI's purpose is to solicit feedback on structuring and enabling partnerships to curate DOE scientific data for AI models; targeted respondents include industry, think tanks, investors, research organizations, and other stakeholders. (From: "Request for Information (RFI) on Partnerships for Transformational Artificial Intelligence Models")

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek input on using DOE data to develop self-improving AI models
rubrics_metrics.description: This RFI also seeks input on using this data to develop self-improving AI models for science and engineering to advance scientific discovery, energy, and national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should provide input on how DOE scientific data could be used to develop self-improving AI models and how those models could advance scientific discovery, energy, and national security. (From same DOE RFI)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete examples, best practices, case studies, and actionable recommendations on AI agent security
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourages respondents to provide concrete examples, best practices, case studies, and actionable recommendations based on their experience developing and deploying AI agent systems and managing and anticipating their attendant risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should be grounded in practical experience and aim to be actionable; submissions may inform CAISI/NIST's evaluation of security risks, vulnerability assessments, development of evaluation and assessment measurements and methods, and technical guidelines. (From: "Request for Information Regarding Security Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Agents")

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify statutes, regulations, and processes that hinder AI development/adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Request input in identifying existing Federal statutes, regulations, agency rules, guidance, forms, and administrative processes that unnecessarily hinder the development, deployment, and adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies within the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSTP seeks submissions that name specific legal or regulatory barriers and explain how they hamper AI innovation or adoption; respondents may include private sector organizations, industry groups, academia, state/local/tribal governments, and other interested parties. (From: "Notice of Request for Information; Regulatory Reform on Artificial Intelligence")

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend priorities for regulatory reform to promote AI innovation and adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Through this RFI, OSTP is seeking input ... on priorities for such regulatory reform or other agency action necessary to promote AI innovation and adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should propose and justify priority actions for reform (e.g., statutes to change, guidance to issue, processes to streamline) aimed at promoting AI innovation and deployment. (From same OSTP RFI)

rubrics_metrics.name: Target respondent groups and inclusivity of responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Many notices explicitly request input from a broad set of stakeholders — including industry, think tanks, investors, research organizations, academia, state, local, and tribal governments, and other interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing comments, note the agencies explicitly invite contributions from this broad list of stakeholders; tailoring responses to the agency's stated stakeholder groups may increase relevance. (Throughout multiple RFIs and notices in the listing)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practices and methodologies for measuring and improving secure development/deployment of AI agent systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeking information and insights on practices and methodologies for measuring and improving the secure development and deployment of AI agent systems, including anticipating exploits like hijacking and backdoor attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should describe measurement approaches, assessment methods, metrics, and concrete practices used to evaluate and improve AI agent security; include case studies or empirical results where possible. (From: CAISI/NIST RFI excerpt)

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute ideas for National AI R&D Strategic Plan updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Welcomes input on how the previous National Artificial Intelligence Research and Development Strategic Plan can be rewritten to accelerate AI-driven innovation, enhance U.S. economic and national security, promote human flourishing, and maintain U.S. AI leadership over the next 3–5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NITRD NCO encourages contributions from AI researchers, industry leaders, and other stakeholders; previously submitted responses to related RFIs may be considered. Comments should focus on priority policy actions and the Federal government's unique R&D role. (From: "Request for Information on the Development of a 2025 National AI R&D Strategic Plan")

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend actions HHS can take to accelerate AI adoption in clinical care
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek broad public comment on what HHS can do to accelerate the adoption and use of AI as part of clinical care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should provide recommendations, evidence, and examples about policies, incentives, technical standards, safety measures, or regulatory approaches that would accelerate responsible clinical use of AI. (From: HHS RFI excerpt)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide input on leveraging DOE lands for AI infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: The DOE is exploring opportunities to leverage its land assets to support the growing demand for AI infrastructure and invites comments on those opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments could address feasibility, environmental and community impacts, technical requirements for data centers, partnerships, and alignment with national AI policy objectives. (From: "Request for Information on Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure on DOE Lands")

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation procedures for public briefings and virtual events
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices announcing public briefings or virtual events provide details on the procedures for participating in the virtual public briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested parties should follow the specific participation procedures (registration, deadlines, contact emails/phone numbers) published in the notice to attend briefings and provide oral comments where allowed. (From: "Public Briefing on Framework for Artificial Intelligence Diffusion" and similar notices)

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of proposed reporting requirements for advanced AI development
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed rule would establish reporting requirements for the development of advanced AI models and computing clusters under BIS Industrial Base Surveys–Data Collections regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities developing advanced AI models or clusters should note potential new reporting obligations and may submit comments on scope, definitions, burden, and confidentiality concerns during the notice-and-comment period. (From: "Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced Artificial Intelligence Models and Computing Clusters")

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent statutory definitions of 'artificial intelligence' where specified
rubrics_metrics.description: Some final priorities and definitions (e.g., Department of Education priority) specify that they use the same AI definition from statute (15 U.S.C. 9401(3)) to maintain consistency in implementation of federal AI policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to or designing programs/grant proposals under these priorities, use the agency-specified statutory definition of AI for consistency. (From: "Final Priority and Definitions—Secretary's Supplemental Priority on Advancing Artificial Intelligence in Education")

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how responses will inform agency work or rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices often state that responses 'may inform' agency activities such as policy development, security assessments, regulatory reform priorities, strategic plans, or technical guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should clearly connect recommendations to anticipated agency actions and, where possible, explain the practical implications of adopting the suggested approaches. (Observed across multiple RFIs and NIST/OSTP/BIS entries)
